title: Ohm's Law
summary: the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance, plus the power-law variants.
body:
ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is proportional to the
voltage across it and inversely proportional to its resistance. combined with
the power law (P = V * I), the three quantities V, I, R and power P can each be
found from any two of the others.

formulas.description: power from voltage across a resistance

examples: 5 V across a 220 ohm resistor: I = 5 / 220 = 22.7 mA, P = 5^2 / 220 = 114 mW (use a >=1/4 W part).
an LED dropping 2 V at 20 mA from 5 V needs R = (5 - 2) / 0.02 = 150 ohm.
gotchas: ohm's law applies to resistive (linear) elements; diodes, LEDs and transistors are non-linear and do not obey it directly
always check resistor power rating: P = I^2 * R can exceed a 1/4 W part quickly at low resistances
